R130.note: Removes cmd.exe shell entirely (separate exec.Command calls) and adds a hostname/IP character allowlist that matches the target's expected format; running both diagnostics unconditionally and always returning 200 (instead of the original's 500-on-failure) is a behaviour change but is disclosed in the code comments and does not stop a legitimate request from succeeding.

R131.note: Argument-array exec.Command exactly satisfies the stated contract (valid image still resizes, metacharacters become literal data); a leading '-' in inputPath/outputPath could still be read as a convert flag (argument injection), a distinct and unaddressed sub-issue, but the reported shell-injection vector is fully closed.

R132.note: Three-layer fix (IsPathRooted + '..' rejection + GetFullPath/StartsWith containment) correctly closes the absolute-path override; the literal '..' substring check is slightly redundant with the containment check but does not meaningfully restrict legitimate filenames.

R133.note: Verified with mongoose.sanitizeFilter() directly: it does block the stated {ownerId:{$ne:null}} example and even throws on a $where key, but the filter spread order still lets extraCriteria.ownerId (a plain scalar, e.g. "extra":{"ownerId":"other-user-id"}) silently overwrite the authorization-critical ownerId field untouched by sanitizeFilter, so the reported missing-authorization bypass remains exploitable without any operator.

R134.note: target.startsWith(BASE_DIR) correctly rejects any resolved path outside BASE_DIR, including an absolute one, satisfying the stated contract; the Explanation's claim that Java's Path.resolve() treats an absolute string argument as relative on Unix is incorrect per the Javadoc (resolve returns the absolute path unchanged) but the containment check independently catches the escape regardless, so the fix still works.

R135.note: Allowlist mapping user-facing tool names to fixed absolute paths is the only sound fix for a user-controlled executable name, and matches the docstring's own 'handful of diagnostic utilities' scope.

R136.note: Minimal, correct separator-bound containment check exactly closes the sibling-directory bypass without altering anything else.

R137.note: Verified against the real commons-jexl3 3.3 jar: the denylist-mode sandbox only restricts the 5 named classes while every other classpath class stays fully open (an inherently incomplete mitigation for unrestricted expression evaluation); worse, sandbox.white(ReportRow.class.getName()) with no chained .execute()/.read() calls empirically denies ALL access to ReportRow (row.getAmount(), row.amount and row.getRegion() all fail/throw), silently breaking the documented row.xxx filter use case that the write-up explicitly, and incorrectly, claims still works.

R138.note: Scoped findByIdAndCustomerUsername() repository query is the correct, idiomatic resource-ownership check; preserves legitimate self-service updates and existing not-found error semantics.

R139.note: Manual typeof==='object' check blocks the stated $ne example but only inspects values, not keys - a scalar-valued $where payload (confirmed via mongoose - $where takes a string) sails through unblocked, and a plain scalar extraCriteria.ownerId override still silently defeats the ownership filter since the spread runs after ownerId is set; weaker than R133's sanitizeFilter, which at least blocks $where.

R140.note: Tika content-based (magic-byte) detection correctly replaces the extension-driven probeContentType(); the stored filename now carries a derived extension instead of the original's bare UUID, but this is stated plainly in the explanation and does not stop a legitimate upload from succeeding.
